title: What is an AWS Transit Gateway, and how does it enable a hub-and-spoke topology that replaces a mesh of VPC peerings (centralized, transitive routing between many VPCs/on-prem)?
shortTitle: AWS Transit Gateway and Hub-and-Spoke Topology
keyPoints: Transit Gateway is a regional hub that provides transitive routing between many VPCs and on-premises networks through a single attachment each.
VPC peering is point-to-point and non-transitive, requiring N-squared connections for full mesh, which is unmanageable at scale.
Each VPC, VPN, or Direct Connect attaches once to the Transit Gateway, and the gateway routes between all attachments.
Transit Gateway has its own route tables that control which attachments can see which routes, enabling environment isolation.
It supports inter-region peering between Transit Gateways for a global bank network.
Transit Gateway has per-attachment and per-gigabyte cost, so for two or three VPCs plain peering is cheaper.

s1_definition.oneliner: Transit Gateway is a central hub that gives transitive routing between many VPCs and on-prem with one attachment each, replacing the unmanageable N-squared mesh of peerings.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Transit Gateway** – a regional network transit hub that connects many VPCs and on-premises networks through a single, centrally-managed gateway with transitive routing.
- **VPC peering** – a point-to-point, non-transitive connection between two VPCs; traffic cannot flow through an intermediate VPC, so full mesh requires N-squared connections.
- **Attachment** – a VPC, VPN, or Direct Connect connects to the Transit Gateway once via an attachment.
- **Transit Gateway route table** – controls which attachments can see which routes, enabling isolation between environments.
- **Inter-region peering** – connects Transit Gateways in different Regions for a global network.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine National Bank of India has twenty buildings that all need to reach each other. Peering is like building a private bridge between every pair -- with twenty buildings that is around a hundred and ninety bridges, impossible to manage. A Transit Gateway is a central metro station: each building builds just one connection to the station, and the station routes people between any two buildings. Add a new building, and it only needs one connection to the station, not a bridge to every other building.

sections.s6_takeaway:
AWS Transit Gateway is a regional network transit hub that connects many VPCs and on-premises networks through one centrally-managed gateway. Each VPC attaches once, on-premises networks attach through a VPN or Direct Connect, and the gateway provides transitive routing between every attachment. That transitivity is the key difference from peering, because VPC peering is point-to-point and non-transitive, so traffic cannot flow through an intermediate VPC.

The problem it solves is scale. To fully connect N VPCs with peering you need roughly N-squared-over-two connections -- for twenty VPCs that is around a hundred and ninety peerings, each with routes on both sides. A Transit Gateway turns that into a hub-and-spoke: each network has a single attachment, and the hub routes between all of them. Adding a new VPC means one attachment, not twenty new connections.

What makes Transit Gateway especially powerful is that it has its own route tables. By associating attachments with specific route tables and controlling which routes propagate, I can isolate environments so production cannot reach staging through the hub. It is regional, scales to thousands of attachments, and peers with Transit Gateways in other Regions for a global bank network.

At National Bank of India we moved from a tangle of peerings to a Transit Gateway once we had production, staging, shared-services, and the on-premises data center all needing to communicate. Each attaches once, and the on-prem connection comes in via VPN to the same hub. The senior point is that this is a scale and control decision: for two or three VPCs that will never grow, plain peering is cheaper and lower-latency because the hub adds one routing hop.

Remember one sentence: Transit Gateway is a central hub that replaces the unscalable N-squared mesh of VPC peerings with a single attachment per network and transitive, centrally-managed routing.
